mainTopic: Hearsay testimony for a בכור, liquids that flow out on שבת, soaking and rinsing salted foods in hot water, and רבי יוחנן's comparisons of בבל and ארץ ישראל
overview: The amud opens by finishing the rule that עד מפי עד is accepted only for עדות אשה. The גמרא then asks whether hearsay is also accepted for a blemished בכור. רב אסי reads the rule as covering any testimony a woman may give, and the הלכה follows him: hearsay is valid for a בכור. Next the גמרא returns to the honeycomb case. Through רב הושעיא's ברייתא and אביי's answer, we learn that רבי אלעזר permits juice that flows out on its own even when a food turns into a liquid. A new משנה teaches that food cooked before שבת may be soaked in hot water on שבת, while uncooked food may only be rinsed. The exception is certain salted fish, for which rinsing completes the cooking, so one who rinses them is חייב חטאת. Along the way come stories about רבי אבא's chicken and Babylonian כותח. A longer story follows: רבי יוחנן scolds students who guessed, and then explains why בבל's birds are fat, why its festivals are joyful, and why its scholars dress distinctively. His answer about why the גוים are contaminated begins here and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Hearsay is accepted only for a woman's testimony
steps.stepSummary: This is the end of a statement that began in the previous section: עד מפי עד is accepted only for עדות אשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: …except for testimony regarding a woman alone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a rule that started in the previous section: hearsay testimony works only in the case of עדות אשה. This rule sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עדות אשה means testimony that a woman's husband has died, so that she may remarry. The חכמים were lenient there to keep her from becoming an עגונה, a woman unable to remarry. This statement limits the leniency of hearsay to that one area.

keyTerms.meaning: Testimony that a woman's husband died, which permits her to remarry

phrases.english: except for testimony regarding a woman alone.
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence that started earlier; the whole line is quoted below as the teaching of דבי מנשיא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a statement begun earlier
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hearsay testimony is valid only for testimony that frees a woman to remarry.

steps.title: Is hearsay accepted for a firstborn animal?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether עד מפי עד is accepted for testimony about a בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: Is hearsay testimony accepted for testimony about a firstborn animal?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new question: does hearsay testimony work for a בכור? This sets up the dispute in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the חורבן, a כהן who wants to eat a blemished בכור must bring witnesses that he did not make the blemish himself. The question is what happens when nobody saw the blemish happen, but someone heard about it from an eyewitness. The issue is whether this second-hand report is good enough.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among them (an open question for the חכמים)
A witness who reports what another witness told him, i.e., hearsay
The firstborn of a kosher animal, which belongs to a כהן

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether the animal is a בכור or whether it has a blemish. The question is only whether hearsay can prove that the כהן did not cause the blemish.

phrases.english: It was asked of them:

phrases.aramaic: עֵד מִפִּי עֵד לְעֵדוּת בְּכוֹר, מַהוּ?
phrases.english: hearsay testimony for testimony about a firstborn animal, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks whether the limit just stated also excludes בכור
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether hearsay testimony is accepted to show that a בכור's blemish was not caused on purpose

steps.title: Two אמוראים disagree
steps.stepSummary: One אמורא forbids hearsay for a בכור and רב אסי permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אמי (some texts read רב אתי) prohibited it, and רב אסי permitted it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports that two אמוראים argued about this question. One says hearsay is not accepted for a בכור, and the other says it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The one who forbids is following the plain meaning of the rule in step 1, that hearsay is only for a woman. רב אסי is lenient, and the next steps show how he defends himself.

keyTerms.meaning: Prohibited, ruled that it is not accepted
Permits, rules that it is accepted

phrases.english: Rav Ami [Rav Itai] prohibited,
phrases.notes: Some versions say רב אמי (in round brackets), and the corrected wording in square brackets is רב אתי. The very next line, though, talks about רב אמי.

phrases.english: and Rav Asi permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַמֵּי אָסַר וְרַב אַסִּי שָׁרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question by presenting a dispute
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is disputed: one forbids hearsay for a בכור and רב אסי permits it.

steps.title: Challenge from the school of מנשיא
steps.stepSummary: רב אמי challenges רב אסי from a ברייתא which says that hearsay is valid only for עדות אשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אמי said to רב אסי: But דבי מנשיא taught: Hearsay testimony is valid only for testimony regarding a woman!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אמי attacks רב אסי's lenient view by quoting a teaching that seems to allow hearsay only for a woman's testimony.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If hearsay is valid only for עדות אשה, then it should not be valid for a בכור. That makes רב אסי's ruling look like it contradicts a ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught! (introduces a challenge from a ברייתא)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַמֵּי לְרַב אַסִּי:
phrases.english: Rav Ami said to Rav Asi:
But didn't the school of Menashya teach:
hearsay testimony is not valid
except for testimony regarding a woman alone!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the lenient view in the dispute
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אסי's ruling that hearsay is accepted for a בכור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא limits hearsay to עדות אשה alone, and a בכור is not עדות אשה.

steps.title: Reread it: any testimony that a woman may give
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי rereads the ברייתא to mean any testimony for which a woman is a valid witness.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: only for testimony for which a woman is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי answers by changing how we read the ברייתא. It does not mean testimony about a woman. It means testimony that a woman herself is allowed to give.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman is a valid witness for a husband's death, and she is also valid for testimony about a בכור's blemish. So under this reading the ברייתא actually includes בכור, and רב אסי's view stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Say instead (introduces a rereading of a text)
For which a woman is a valid witness

steps.confusionAlert: The change is from testimony ABOUT a woman to testimony that a woman is ABLE TO GIVE. This one shift is what lets בכור into the rule.

phrases.english: Say: for testimony for which a woman
is valid, alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא limits hearsay to testimony about a woman's marital status.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא allows hearsay in any area where a woman is a valid witness, and that includes בכור.

steps.title: רב יימר ruled hearsay valid for a בכור
steps.stepSummary: רב יימר actually relied on hearsay to permit a blemished בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יימר deemed hearsay testimony valid for a firstborn animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports a real ruling: רב יימר accepted hearsay testimony for a בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a practical case that follows רב אסי's lenient view. It sets up מרימר's reaction in the next step.

phrases.english: Rav Yeimar deemed valid
hearsay testimony for a firstborn.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the lenient view being applied in practice
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hearsay was accepted in practice for a בכור.

steps.title: מרימר mocks the lenient ruling
steps.stepSummary: מרימר disapproved and nicknamed him 'יימר who permits the firstborn.'
steps.simpleTranslation: מרימר called him: יימר who permits firstborns.
steps.whatsHappening: מרימר criticizes רב יימר's ruling by giving him a mocking nickname.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The nickname shows that מרימר held that hearsay is not valid for a בכור. In his view, רב יימר was wrongly permitting animals that should stay forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Called him, applied a description to him

phrases.english: Mareimar called him:
Yeimar who permits the firstborn.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב יימר's ruling
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב יימר's practical acceptance of hearsay for a בכור
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: מרימר held that hearsay is not valid for a בכור.

steps.title: Final ruling: hearsay is valid for a בכור
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה is that עד מפי עד is valid for a בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: hearsay testimony is valid for a firstborn.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final halacha, which follows the lenient view of רב אסי and רב יימר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Despite מרימר's criticism, the halacha accepts hearsay for a בכור. This fits רב אסי's rereading of the ברייתא of דבי מנשיא.
steps.whatToRemember: עד מפי עד is accepted wherever a woman is a valid witness. That includes the death of a husband and the blemish of a בכור. The halacha follows this view.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical ruling about which kinds of testimony a בית דין may rely on.

phrases.english: And the halacha is: hearsay testimony
is valid for a firstborn.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides against מרימר
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Hearsay testimony is valid for a בכור.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: honeycombs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words חלות דבש to begin a new topic.
steps.simpleTranslation: Honeycombs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה and quotes the words 'honeycombs' as a heading. This is a setup line for the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה taught that according to רבי אלעזר, honey that flows on its own from honeycombs on שבת is permitted. The גמרא is about to bring a related ברייתא.

phrases.english: Honeycombs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of testimony and returns to the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces the משנה's case of honey flowing from honeycombs on שבת.

steps.title: רב הושעיא brings a ברייתא about crushed olives and grapes
steps.stepSummary: רב הושעיא brings a ברייתא: juice that flows on its own on שבת from olives and grapes crushed before שבת is forbidden. רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון permit it.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב הושעיא came from נהרדעא, he brought a ברייתא with him: Olives and grapes that one crushed before שבת, and their juice came out on its own, are prohibited. רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון permit.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הושעיא arrives with a ברייתא about a case similar to the honeycombs. The case is fruit crushed before שבת whose juice flows out by itself on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion forbids the juice, even though nobody did anything on שבת. רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון permit it, which matches the lenient view of the honey case in the משנה. The ברייתא extends the dispute from honey to olives and grapes.

keyTerms.meaning: When [so-and-so] came (usually from another place, bringing a teaching)

steps.confusionAlert: The crushing happened before שבת. The only question is whether juice that drips out on its own during שבת may be used.

phrases.english: When Rav Hoshaya came from Neharde'a,
he came and brought a baraita in his hand:
olives and grapes that one crushed on Shabbat eve,
and [the juices] came out on their own, are prohibited.
And Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon permit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that relates to the משנה's honeycomb case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Juice that flows on its own on שבת from olives and grapes crushed before שבת is forbidden according to the first opinion. רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון permit it.

steps.title: What does the ברייתא add beyond an extra name?
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף challenges רב הושעיא's ברייתא: it seems to teach nothing new except adding רבי שמעון's name.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Did he only come to teach us one extra person?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף questions why רב הושעיא bothered to quote his ברייתא. Our משנה already taught this leniency in the name of רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה about honeycombs (חלות דבש) already said that רבי אלעזר permits what seeps out on its own. The only new thing in the ברייתא seems to be that רבי שמעון agrees. רב יוסף is saying, 'Is that all?'

keyTerms.meaning: An extra person (one more name of a scholar who holds the view)

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Did he come to teach us an extra person?
phrases.notes: He's not really asking; the only new thing here seems to be רבי שמעון's name.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the ברייתא quoted in step 10.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא repeats רבי אלעזר's leniency from the משנה. Its only addition is one more name.

steps.title: אביי: the ברייתא teaches a new case, food that turns into liquid
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the ברייתא teaches a lot. Honey stays a food, but olives and grapes turn into a liquid, and רבי אלעזר is lenient even there.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: It teaches us a lot. From the משנה alone I would have said that the leniency applies only there, where the item began as food and ended as food. But here, where it began as food and ended as liquid, I would say no. So the ברייתא teaches us that he is lenient here too.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends the ברייתא. He shows that it teaches a new case the משנה did not cover.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Honey that seeps from a honeycomb can still be called food, so the משנה's leniency might be limited to that. Juice from olives and grapes is a real liquid that came out of a food. The ברייתא shows that רבי אלעזר permits even that.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches us a great deal
I would have thought (an early, mistaken assumption)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אלעזר, juice that seeps out on its own is permitted even when it changes from a food into a liquid.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
It is teaching us a great deal,
for if we had only the Mishnah, I would have said:
It is there that it is permitted,
because at first it was food and in the end it is still food (honey),

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא דְּמֵעִיקָּרָא אוּכְלָא וּלְבַסּוֹף מַשְׁקֶה —
phrases.english: but here, where at first it was food and in the end it is liquid (olives and grapes),
I might say it is not permitted,
so it teaches us that it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's challenge from step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the ברייתא teaches a new case (חידוש), not just a new name
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אלעזר is lenient only when the item stays a food, like honey.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אלעזר is lenient even when a food turns into a liquid, like olive and grape juice.

steps.title: משנה: soaking food already cooked, rinsing food not yet cooked
steps.stepSummary: Food that was put in hot water before שבת may be soaked in hot water on שבת. Food that was not may only be rinsed.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Anything that was put in hot water before שבת may be soaked in hot water on שבת. Anything that was not put in hot water before שבת may be rinsed with hot water on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new topic: using hot water on salted foods on שבת. It contrasts food that was already cooked with food that was not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once a food has been cooked, soaking it in hot water does not cook it again, so soaking is allowed. If it was never cooked, soaking could cook it. A quick rinse, however, is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Was put in hot water (already cooked)

steps.confusionAlert: Soaking (שרייה) and rinsing (הדחה) are not the same. Soaking means leaving the food in the water and is allowed only for food that was already cooked. Rinsing is a quick pour and is allowed even for food that was not cooked.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
Anything that was put in hot water before Shabbat,
one may soak it in hot water on Shabbat.

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל שֶׁלֹּא בָּא בְּחַמִּין מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת —
phrases.english: And anything that was not put in hot water before Shabbat,
one may rinse it with hot water on Shabbat,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Food cooked before שבת may be soaked in hot water on שבת. Food not cooked may only be rinsed.

steps.title: משנה's exception: fish for which rinsing finishes the cooking
steps.stepSummary: Old salted fish, small salted fish, and קוליאס האיספנין may not even be rinsed with hot water, because rinsing finishes preparing them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Except for old salted fish, small salted fish, and the Spanish קוליאס fish, because rinsing them is the completion of their preparation.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה names exceptions to the rinsing permission. These fish may not be rinsed with hot water on שבת at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These fish are so soft that a hot rinse is enough to make them ready to eat. Since the rinse does the final step of the work, it counts as cooking (בישול). That is forbidden on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: The completion of their preparation (here, of cooking)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a small act counts as a forbidden מלאכה if it is the act that finishes the work.

phrases.english: except for old salted fish
and small salted fish
and the Spanish kolyas fish,
since rinsing them is itself the completion of their preparation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the rinsing permission from step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rinsing these fish with hot water on שבת is forbidden, because the rinse completes their cooking.

steps.title: What kind of cooked food would still need soaking?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a real example of an already-cooked food that someone would soak in hot water.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Like what?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for an example of the משנה's first case. Why would anyone soak food that is already cooked?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cooked food is normally ready to eat. The גמרא wants a case where soaking an already-cooked item actually makes sense.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Like what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for an example of the first rule in step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A practical case of already-cooked food that someone would soak in hot water.

steps.title: Example: רבי אבא's chicken
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא answers that the example is רבי אבא's chicken, which was cooked until it completely fell apart.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ספרא said: Like the chicken of רבי אבא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא gives the example. רבי אבא's chicken was cooked first and then soaked in hot water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For health reasons, רבי אבא's chicken was cooked until it dissolved, then soaked again in hot water. Since it was cooked before שבת, the soaking may be done on שבת.

phrases.english: Rav Safra said:
Like the chicken of Rabbi Abba.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אבא's chicken, which was cooked thoroughly and then soaked in hot water.

steps.title: רב ספרא's story of eating Rabbi Abba's chicken
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא tells that he once ate this chicken and would have vomited if רבי אבא had not given him three-year-old wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב ספרא said: Once I visited there, and he fed me some of it. If רבי אבא had not given me three-year-old wine to drink, I would have vomited.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a side story, not a new law. It shows how unpleasant the dissolved chicken was to someone from בבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story shows what this dish was like: mushy and hard to stomach. Only strong, aged wine helped רב ספרא keep it down.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have been forced to vomit

phrases.english: And Rav Safra said:
One time I happened to come there,
and he fed me some of it,
and if not for Rabbi Abba
giving me three-leaf (three-year-old) wine to drink,
I would have been forced to vomit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a personal story about the chicken from step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No law. A story describing how unpleasant רבי אבא's chicken was.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's disgust at Babylonian כותח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reports that רבי יוחנן would spit just at the thought of Babylonian כותח, a dip made with sour milk.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן would spit at the mention of Babylonian כותח.
steps.whatsHappening: The side discussion continues. Now a food from בבל is shown to disgust a sage from ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets up a comparison. Each land found the other land's food disgusting. It prepares for רב יוסף's reply in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A Babylonian dip made from sour milk, bread crusts, and salt

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan would spit
at the thought of the Babylonians' kutach.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of disgusting foods from step 17, now from the other side.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No law. רבי יוחנן found Babylonian כותח disgusting.

steps.title: רב יוסף's reply: we should spit at רבי אבא's chicken
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף replies that if רבי יוחנן spits at כותח, the people of בבל have more reason to spit at רבי אבא's chicken.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Then we should spit at רבי אבא's chicken!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף pushes back against רבי יוחנן's disgust. He turns the complaint around.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He argues that taste is local. Food from ארץ ישראל can be just as disgusting to people from בבל. So רבי יוחנן's spitting does not prove that כותח is worse.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Then let us spit at the chicken of Rabbi Abba!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יוחנן's reaction in step 18 by pointing to the chicken from step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's disgust at Babylonian כותח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Babylonians find רבי אבא's chicken equally disgusting, so the dislike is just a matter of local taste.

steps.title: רב גזא: the sick of ארץ ישראל asked for כותח
steps.stepSummary: רב גזא adds a proof: when he made כותח in ארץ ישראל, all the sick people there asked him for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, רב גזא said: Once I visited there and made Babylonian כותח, and all the sick people of the West (ארץ ישראל) asked me for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for רב יוסף's side. Not everyone in ארץ ישראל disliked כותח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ועוד ('and furthermore') adds a second point. In ארץ ישראל itself, sick people wanted כותח, which shows it had real value. So רבי יוחנן's disgust was a personal taste, not a sign that the food was bad.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה allows soaking food in hot water on שבת only if it was cooked before שבת. The stories about the chicken and the כותח are a light side discussion about local tastes.

phrases.english: And furthermore, Rav Gaza said:
One time I happened to come there (to Eretz Yisrael),
and I made Babylonian kutach,
and all the sick people of the West asked me for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב יוסף's reply in step 19.
steps.raayaObject: That Babylonian כותח is not truly disgusting
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב גזא's story: the sick people of ארץ ישראל asked him for כותח.

steps.title: What if someone rinsed the forbidden fish?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about foods not cooked in hot water and asks what the law is if someone rinsed the excluded fish.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'Anything that was not cooked in hot water before שבת may be rinsed in hot water, except old salted fish and קוליים האיספנין.' The גמרא asks: if someone did rinse them, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and asks a question about it. If a person rinsed the fish that the משנה said not to rinse, how serious is it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only told us not to rinse these fish. It did not say how bad it is if someone does. The גמרא wants to know: is it a full Torah-level מלאכה that needs a חטאת, or only a smaller prohibition?

keyTerms.meaning: Etc. (the quote continues in the משנה)

phrases.english: Anything that did not come into hot water, etc.
If he rinsed, what is the law?
phrases.notes: Refers to the salted fish that the משנה excludes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about רבי אבא's chicken and כותח and returns to the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How serious is it if someone rinsed old salted fish or קוליים האיספנין in hot water on שבת?

steps.title: רב יוסף: rinsing makes one liable to a חטאת
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף rules that someone who rinsed these fish must bring a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: If he rinsed them, he is obligated to bring a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the question. Rinsing these fish counts as a real Torah-level מלאכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These fish are almost ready to eat. Hot water finishes softening them, so rinsing completes the cooking. That makes it a full act of בישול (cooking), which needs a חטאת when done by mistake.

keyTerms.meaning: Obligated to bring a sin-offering (for a Torah prohibition done by mistake)

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
If he rinsed, he is liable to a sin-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Rinsing these fish is a Torah-level act of cooking, so one is חייב חטאת.

steps.title: Proof from the משנה's wording
steps.stepSummary: מר בריה דרבינא shows that the משנה itself calls rinsing these fish the 'completion of their work.'
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בריה דרבינא said: We also learned this in the משנה: 'Except for old salted fish and קוליים האיספנין, because rinsing them is the completion of their work.'
steps.whatsHappening: מר בריה דרבינא brings support for רב יוסף. The משנה's own words show that rinsing these fish is a full מלאכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'גמר מלאכתן' means rinsing finishes the cooking. Finishing a מלאכה is a full Torah-level act. So the משנה already teaches what רב יוסף said.

keyTerms.meaning: We too have learned this (a proof from a known source)
A type of Spanish salted fish (tuna)
The completion of their work (the finishing step of cooking)

phrases.english: Mar, son of Ravina, said:
We too have learned this:
Except for old salted fish and Spanish kolyas,
since their rinsing is the completion of their work.
phrases.notes: 'Completion of their work' is the wording used for a full מלאכה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב יוסף's ruling from the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's ruling that rinsing these fish needs a חטאת
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's words 'שהדחתן זו היא גמר מלאכתן'

steps.title: Conclusion: the proof stands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא agrees with the proof. The law follows רב יוסף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'שמע מינה' closes the discussion with no challenge. Rinsing these fish on שבת is a full Torah-level מלאכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this (the proof is accepted)

steps.whatToRemember: Rinsing old salted fish in hot water on שבת finishes their cooking. It is a Torah-level מלאכה, so one who does it by mistake is חייב חטאת.

phrases.english: Learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the proof of step 23.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: One who rinses these fish on שבת is חייב חטאת.

steps.title: Setting the scene: רבי יוחנן dozes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a story. Two students sit before רבי יוחנן while he dozes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא and רבי אסי were sitting before רבי יוחנן, and רבי יוחנן was sitting and dozing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a story. It continues the earlier theme of comparing בבל and ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing is ruled here. The detail that רבי יוחנן was dozing matters, because the students speak freely and he later wakes up and reacts.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba was sitting
and Rabbi Asi, before Rabbi Yoḥanan,
and Rabbi Yoḥanan was sitting and dozing.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵיב רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא וְרַבִּי אַסִּי קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a story linked to the earlier comparison of בבל and ארץ ישראל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling. This is the setup of a story.

steps.title: Why are the birds of בבל fat?
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא asks why the birds in בבל are fat. רבי אסי rejects the claim and says the desert of עזה has fatter ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said to רבי אסי: Why are the birds in בבל fat? He answered: Go to the desert of עזה and I will show you birds fatter than them.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the first of four questions. רבי אסי does not explain the fact. He denies it and says ארץ ישראל has fatter birds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of giving a reason, רבי אסי attacks the starting assumption. Birds in ארץ ישראל can be just as fat, so there is nothing to explain.

keyTerms.meaning: The desert of עזה in ארץ ישראל

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא לְרַבִּי אַסִּי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said to Rabbi Asi:
Why are the birds in Babylonia fat?
He said to him: Go to the desert of Gaza
and I will show you fatter ones than them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The first question and answer in the story.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The premise is wrong. The birds of the desert of עזה are even fatter.

steps.title: Why are the יום טוב days in בבל so joyous?
steps.stepSummary: Asked why festivals in בבל are happier, רבי אסי answers that the people there are poor.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why are the festivals in בבל joyous? Because they are poor.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second question and answer. רבי אסי says the people of בבל are poor all year, so the plenty of יום טוב makes them especially happy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their joy comes from contrast. Those who rarely have enough feel a big difference when a festival brings good food.

phrases.english: Why are the festivals in Babylonia joyous?
Because they are poor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second question and answer in the same conversation.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They are poor, so the plenty of יום טוב brings them extra joy.

steps.title: Why do the scholars of בבל dress differently?
steps.stepSummary: Asked why the תלמידי חכמים of בבל are marked out by their clothing, רבי אסי answers that they are not truly learned.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why are the תלמידי חכמים in בבל distinguished? Because they are not people of Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the third question and answer. רבי אסי says the scholars of בבל wear special clothing because their learning alone would not earn them respect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'מצויינין' means they stand out by their dress. רבי אסי's sharp answer is that outward signs make up for what is missing inside.

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי מָה תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים שֶׁבְּבָבֶל מְצוּיָּינִין?
phrases.english: Why are the Torah scholars in Babylonia distinguished?
Because they are not people of Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפְּנֵי מָה תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים שֶׁבְּבָבֶל מְצוּיָּינִין?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The third question and answer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They are not truly learned, so they need special dress to be respected.

steps.title: Why are the גוים morally impure?
steps.stepSummary: Asked why גוים are 'מזוהמים', רבי אסי answers that it comes from eating forbidden creatures.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why are the גוים impure? Because they eat abominable creatures and crawling things.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the fourth and last question and answer. רבי אסי links the bad nature of the גוים to the forbidden food they eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that what a person eats shapes his character. The next step shows that רבי יוחנן does not accept answers like these when they are only guesses.

phrases.english: Why are the gentiles impure?
Because they eat abominable creatures and crawling things.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The fourth and final question and answer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Eating forbidden creatures corrupts their character.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן wakes up and scolds his students
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן wakes and rebukes them: only say something if you are as sure of it as you are that your sister is forbidden to you.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן woke up and said to them: Children! Didn't I tell you that 'Say to wisdom, you are my sister' means: if a matter is as clear to you as the fact that your sister is forbidden to you, say it. If not, don't say it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן rejects all of רבי אסי's answers. They were guesses, and a תלמיד חכם should only say what he is truly sure of.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads the פסוק in משלי as a rule of honesty. Wisdom should be as certain to you as the fact that your sister is forbidden to you. Since the students' answers were not that certain, they should not have said them.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Say to wisdom: you are my sister' (משלי ז:ד)

steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches a lasting rule about learning: do not present a guess as a sure answer.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan woke up because of them,
he said to them: Children!
Did I not say this to you:
'Say to wisdom: You are my sister' —
if the matter is clear to you
like your sister, that she is forbidden to you —
say it, and if not, do not say it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects all four answers given by רבי אסי.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: All of רבי אסי's answers in steps 26-29
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The answers were guesses, not things the students knew with certainty.

steps.title: The students ask רבי יוחנן for real answers
steps.stepSummary: The students ask רבי יוחנן to tell them the answer to one of the questions.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Then let the master tell us one of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The students accept the rebuke and ask רבי יוחנן to answer one of the questions himself. This sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If their guesses were not good enough, they want a reliable answer from their teacher. רבי יוחנן goes on to answer all four questions: the birds (step 32), the festivals (step 38), the scholars (step 43), and the גוים (step 46).

keyTerms.meaning: Then let the master tell us

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: וְלֵימָא לַן מָר אֵיזֶה מֵהֶן?
phrases.english: They said to him: Then let the master tell us some of them?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: וְלֵימָא לַן מָר אֵיזֶה מֵהֶן?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רבי יוחנן's rebuke by asking for proper answers.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The true reason behind at least one of the four questions.

steps.title: The birds of בבל are fat because they were never exiled
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that the birds of בבל are fat because they never went into exile, and proves it from a פסוק about מואב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why are the birds of בבל fat? Because they were not exiled, as it says: 'מואב has been at ease since his youth, he has rested on his lees, and he did not go into exile.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the first question. Unlike רבי אסי, he accepts that the birds of בבל are fatter and gives a reason based on a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in ירמיה describes מואב as strong and settled because it never went into exile, like wine left resting on its sediment. Exile weakens a creature, while staying in one place keeps its strength. The birds of בבל were never exiled, so they stayed fat.

phrases.english: Why are the birds in Babylonia fat —
because they were not exiled, as it is said:
'Moab has been at ease since his youth
and he has rested on his lees
and he did not go into exile.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the students' request and replaces רבי אסי's answer from step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The birds of בבל never went into exile, so they kept their strength and fat (based on the פסוק about מואב).

steps.title: Where do we see that the birds of ארץ ישראל were exiled?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source that the birds and animals of ארץ ישראל went into exile.
steps.simpleTranslation: And here, how do we know that they were exiled?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן's answer assumes that the birds of ארץ ישראל were exiled. The גמרא asks where we see this, and the next step will bring the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We know the people of ארץ ישראל were exiled. But the explanation only works if the birds and animals left too, so that needs a source.

phrases.english: And here, from where do we know that they were exiled?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the assumption behind רבי יוחנן's answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that the birds and animals of ארץ ישראל went into exile.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: even the animals left יהודה for 52 years
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא of רבי יהודה says no one passed through יהודה for 52 years, based on a פסוק saying birds and animals fled. The number comes from the גימטריא of בהמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי יהודה says, for fifty-two years no person passed through יהודה, as it says: 'On the mountains I will raise weeping and wailing... from the bird of the heavens to the animal, they have fled and gone.' The word 'בהמה' adds up in גימטריא to fifty-two.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the proof. The פסוק says even the birds and the animals fled the land, so they too went into exile.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in ירמיה ט:ט says 'from the bird of the heavens to the animal, they have fled and gone,' so the birds of ארץ ישראל were exiled. רבי יהודה also learns the length of that emptiness from the word בהמה: ב(2)+ה(5)+מ(40)+ה(5)=52 years. This supports רבי יוחנן's explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: Counting the number value of a word's letters
Animal; its letters add up to 52

steps.confusionAlert: The 52 years come only from the גימטריא of בהמה. The proof that the birds were exiled comes from the words 'מעוף השמים... נדדו הלכו.'
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's lesson is to say only what you are sure of. His answer: the birds of בבל are fat because they were never exiled, while the birds of ארץ ישראל fled during the 52 years the land was empty.

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:
For fifty-two years
no person passed through Judea, as it is said:
'For the mountains I will raise weeping and wailing, etc.
from the bird of the heavens to the animal
they have fled and gone,'
'Behema' in numerical value
is fifty-two.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 33 by bringing a ברייתא as the source.
steps.raayaObject: That the birds and animals of ארץ ישראל went into exile
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי יהודה on ירמיה ט:ט ('מעוף השמים ועד בהמה נדדו הלכו'), with the גימטריא of בהמה = 52

steps.title: All the fish returned except the קולייס
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב quotes רבי יוחנן: all the exiled creatures (animals, birds and even fish) returned to ארץ ישראל except the קולייס האיספנין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב said in the name of רבי יוחנן: They all came back, except for the קולייס האיספנין fish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a statement that continues the exile theme from the last step. The animals, the birds and even the fish went into exile, and all of them came back except one kind of fish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 34 showed that the birds and animals of ארץ ישראל went into exile. Now we hear that they all returned, together with the fish, which had also gone into exile, with one exception. This explains why that particular fish is still found in בבל.

keyTerms.meaning: A type of fish, the 'Spanish קולייס' (a kind of tuna)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ya'akov said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
They all returned,
phrases.notes: The animals, birds and fish that went into exile came back to ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: except for the kolyas ha'ispanin.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן כּוּלָּן חָזְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Says the exiled birds and animals returned, adds the fish, and names one exception.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All the exiled creatures, including the fish, returned to ארץ ישראל except the קולייס האיספנין.

steps.title: How the fish returned and why the kolyas could not
steps.stepSummary: רב teaches that underground channels carry water from בבל back to עין עיטם. The קולייס has a weak spine, so it could not swim up them.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב said: These slopes of בבל send water back to the spring of עיטם. This fish has a weak spine, so it could not climb up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support from רב to explain how the fish could return, and why one kind did not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב teaches that water flows from בבל back to עין עיטם in ארץ ישראל through underground channels. That gives the fish a route home. The קולייס's spine is not strong enough to swim against that uphill flow, so it stayed behind in בבל.

keyTerms.meaning: The spring of Eitam in ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: As Rav said:
Those inclines of Babylonia
return the water to the spring of Eitam.
phrases.notes: The water travels through underground channels, and the fish returned along with it.

phrases.english: And this fish, since its spine is not strong,
it cannot go up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the mechanism behind step 35's claim.
steps.raayaObject: That the fish returned to ארץ ישראל but the kolyas did not
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's statement about water flowing from בבל to עין עיטם
steps.whatToRemember: The fish went into exile and returned through water channels. Only the weak-spined קולייס stayed in בבל.

steps.title: Why are the festivals in בבל so joyful?
steps.stepSummary: The next question: why are the festivals in בבל more joyous?
steps.simpleTranslation: Why are the festivals in בבל joyful?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to another of the students' questions. This line sets up רבי יוחנן's next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The festivals in בבל felt happier than the festivals in ארץ ישראל. The question asks what causes this difference.

phrases.english: For what reason are the Festivals in Babylonia joyous?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new question from the set the students asked.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the festivals in בבל are more joyful

steps.title: בבל was not included in the curse on festivals
steps.stepSummary: The festivals in בבל are joyous because בבל was not part of the curse. The curse appears in two פסוקים about festivals being stopped and hated.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because they were not part of that curse. As it says: 'I will stop all her joy, her festival, her new moon, her שבת, and all her festivals.' It also says: 'My soul hates your new moons and festivals; they are a burden to Me.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers. ארץ ישראל was cursed so that its festivals would lose their joy, and בבל was not part of that curse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in הושע says that ה׳ will stop the joy of 'her' festivals, meaning ארץ ישראל's. The פסוק in ישעיה adds that those festivals became a 'burden' to ה׳. Since בבל was not included, its festivals stayed happy.

keyTerms.meaning: And I will cause to cease

phrases.english: Because they were not included in that curse,
as it is written: 'And I will cause all her joy to cease,'
her Festival, her New Moon, her Shabbat, and all her Festivals.'
And it is written: 'Your New Moons and your Festivals My soul hates;'
they are a burden upon Me.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 37.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בבל was not included in the curse that took away the joy of ארץ ישראל's festivals.

steps.title: What does 'a burden to Me' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the phrase 'they are a burden to Me' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'they are a burden upon Me' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to clarify a puzzling phrase from the פסוק it just quoted. This sets up רבי אלעזר's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is hard to understand how anything could be a 'burden' to ה׳. The גמרא asks for the meaning of this wording.

phrases.english: What is the meaning of 'they are a burden upon Me'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies a phrase from the פסוק quoted in step 38.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of 'a burden' in the פסוק

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: the burden of choosing a harsh decree
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that ה׳ says: Israel's sinning is bad enough, but they also 'burden' Me to decide which harsh decree to bring on them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said: Isn't it enough that Israel sins before Me? They also make Me work to figure out which harsh decree to bring upon them!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר explains the 'burden.' The sins of the Jewish people force ה׳ to decide how to punish them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'burden' is not tiredness. It describes the sad situation where sin forces punishment. This links back to the festivals: the decrees often struck on festivals, which is why ארץ ישראל's festivals lost their joy.

keyTerms.meaning: The Holy One, Blessed be He
Is it not enough for them

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
Is it not enough for Israel that they sin before Me,
that they also burden Me to know
which harsh decree I will bring upon them!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the clarifying question of step 39.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'burden' is the need to choose which harsh decree to bring on Israel because of their sins.

steps.title: Real-life examples: troops and officials on every festival
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק and רבי חנינא show the curse in action: on every festival, Roman troops came to ציפורי and officials came to טבריה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: There was never a festival when troops did not come to ציפורי. And רבי חנינא said: There was never a festival when an אגמון, a קמטון, and a branch-bearer did not come to טבריה.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give real examples of how the curse ruined festivals in ארץ ישראל. Government troops and tax officials showed up on every festival.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These statements show what 'I will stop her joy' looked like in practice. Searches and tax collection on every רגל destroyed the festive mood in cities like ציפורי and טבריה. בבל did not suffer this, which supports the answer in step 38.

keyTerms.meaning: A troop of soldiers that conducts searches
ציפורי, a city in the גליל
'Branch-bearer,' an official who carried a rod of authority

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzḥak said:
There is not a single Festival
on which troops did not come to Tzippori.
And Rabbi Ḥanina said:
There is not a single Festival
on which there did not come to Tiberias
an egmon, a kamton, and a branch-bearer.
phrases.notes: Roman officials who came to collect taxes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק אֵין לְךָ כׇּל רֶגֶל וָרֶגֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the curse described in steps 38 and 40.
steps.raayaObject: That the festivals of ארץ ישראל were cursed and lost their joy
steps.raayaSupportSource: The historical testimony of רבי יצחק and רבי חנינא about ציפורי and טבריה
steps.whatToRemember: בבל's festivals were joyful because the curse struck ארץ ישראל's festivals, where troops and tax officials came on every רגל.

steps.title: Why do בבל's תלמידי חכמים dress distinctively?
steps.stepSummary: The next question: why are the תלמידי חכמים of בבל distinguished by special clothing?
steps.simpleTranslation: Why are the תלמידי חכמים in בבל marked out (by their clothing)?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to another of the students' questions. This line sets up the answer that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תלמידי חכמים of בבל wore special garments that made them stand out. The question asks why they needed this.

keyTerms.meaning: Distinguished / marked out (here, by their dress)

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי מָה תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים שֶׁבְּבָבֶל מְצוּיָּינִין? —
phrases.english: For what reason are the Torah scholars in Babylonia distinguished?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפְּנֵי מָה תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים שֶׁבְּבָבֶל מְצוּיָּינִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new question from the set the students asked.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the תלמידי חכמים of בבל dress distinctively

steps.title: They are not natives, so clothing earns them respect
steps.stepSummary: Since the scholars are not native to בבל, they are not known by name, so their clothing shows their status. A folk saying backs this up.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because they are not natives of that place. As people say: In my own town, my name; outside my town, my clothes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers. Strangers are not recognized by name, so they need distinctive clothing to be honored.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In your hometown, people respect you because they know who you are. Where you are a newcomer, people only see how you dress. The scholars of בבל came from elsewhere, so their special garb showed who they were.

phrases.english: Because they are not natives of their place.
As people say:
In my own town, my name;
phrases.notes: At home I am honored because of my name.

phrases.english: not in my town, my clothing.
phrases.notes: Elsewhere I am honored because of my clothes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 42.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The scholars are not native to בבל, so their clothing is what earns them recognition.

steps.title: רב יוסף praises בבל's scholars from a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains the פסוק 'יעקב will take root, Israel will bud and blossom' as referring to the תלמידי חכמים of בבל, who add buds and blossoms to the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Those who come, יעקב will take root; Israel will bud and blossom.' רב יוסף taught: These are the תלמידי חכמים of בבל, who make buds and blossoms for the תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds praise for the scholars of בבל. רב יוסף reads a פסוק as describing them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After explaining that these scholars are 'newcomers' to בבל, the גמרא shows that this is not a weakness. The 'ones who come' into exile took root and made the תורה blossom with new insights.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who come (here, the ones who went into exile)

phrases.english: 'Those who come, Jacob will take root;'
Israel will bud and blossom.'
Rav Yosef taught:
These are the Torah scholars in Babylonia,
who make buds and blossoms for the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַבָּאִים יַשְׁרֵשׁ יַעֲקֹב יָצִיץ וּפָרַח יִשְׂרָאֵל תָּנֵי רַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds praise for the scholars discussed in step 43.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק about Israel budding and blossoming refers to the תלמידי חכמים of בבל, who enrich the תורה.
steps.whatToRemember: The scholars of בבל were newcomers who dressed distinctively, and they made the תורה flourish.

steps.title: Why are the nations contaminated?
steps.stepSummary: The next question: why are גוים spiritually and morally contaminated?
steps.simpleTranslation: Why are גוים contaminated?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another question. This line sets up the answer, which continues into the next passage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'contaminated' refers to a spiritual and moral impurity. The question asks for its source.

phrases.english: For what reason are gentiles contaminated?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new question in the series answered by רבי יוחנן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source of the spiritual contamination of the nations

steps.title: Because they did not stand at הר סיני
steps.stepSummary: The answer begins: the nations did not stand at הר סיני. The explanation of why that matters continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because they did not stand on הר סיני. For at the time when...
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן begins his answer: the nations were not present at מתן תורה. The sentence continues into the next passage, which explains what happened at that moment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Standing at הר סיני had a cleansing effect, which the next passage will spell out. Those who were not there did not receive this purification.

keyTerms.meaning: Mount Sinai, where the תורה was given

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence is cut off at 'שֶׁבְּשָׁעָה'. The full explanation of what happened at הר סיני comes on the next amud, so don't treat this step as the complete answer.

phrases.english: Because they did not stand on Mount Sinai.
For at the time when
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to step 45.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The nations are contaminated because they did not stand at הר סיני (explanation continues on the next amud).
